arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 after a phishing campaign led to execution of a malicious PowerShell payload from Outlook. The payload deployed a C2 beacon via rundll32.exe using a DLL from the Temp directory. The external C2 server (185.220.101.42) was previously observed conducting Nmap scans. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall and resetting the user's credentials and MFA token. No lateral movement or data exfiltration was detected. The host was scanned and cleaned of a low-severity PUP. Reconciliation note: external management IP 203.0.113.40 from decommissioned asset M2-5200 was included for tracking.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 observed conducting Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15).
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
Malicious encoded PowerShell command executed under user context, spawned from Outlook.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443.
Incident response initiated based on EDR alerts for suspicious process chain and C2 traffic.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 185.220.101.42.
User CORP\jsmith's password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-AP01 completed; PUP.Optional.BrowserHelper detected and quarantined.
Incident containment verified. Host returned to service with user re-enrolled.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01, where user CORP\jsmith was targeted via a phishing campaign. An encoded PowerShell command launched from Outlook initiated a malicious process chain involving rundll32.exe loading an unsigned DLL from the Temp directory, establishing C2 communication over HTTPS to 198.51.100.23. Indicators match Cobalt Strike beaconing. Lateral movement attempts were observed via SMB to WS-FIN-50. The external scanning IP 185.220.101.42 was previously observed conducting Nmap scans. The host was scanned and cleaned, and the user's credentials and MFA were reset. Asset M2-5200 (203.0.113.40) is referenced for reconciliation.

Incident response completed: user credentials and MFA reset, host scanned and cleaned.

arguments.summary: Credential compromise on host WS-FIN-AP01 initiated via phishing email with malicious macro leading to PowerShell execution and DLL sideloading. Attacker established C2 beacon to external IP 185.220.101.42. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall and resetting user credentials. No lateral movement or data exfiltration observed. Decommissioned asset reference 203.0.113.40 reconciled per M2-5200.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted Nmap SYN scan against internal host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Logged by IDS.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.

arguments.summary: A critical lateral movement incident was initiated from an external IP address (45.33.32.156), identified as a known scanning host. The threat actor performed a network scan against an internal IT workstation (10.0.2.15) and leveraged valid credentials (CORP\helpdesk) to authenticate and move laterally into the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet. The compromised host was secured via password and MFA reset, firewall block on the origin IP, full EPP scan (clean), and system hardening via Ansible. No malware was detected. The asset record M2-5201 decommissioning reference (203.0.113.41) is included for reconciliation.

arguments.summary: Lateral movement detected originating from external IP 45.33.32.156, which conducted an Nmap SYN scan against host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). The scan triggered low-severity IDS alerts. Further investigation revealed no malicious payloads or active compromise. Host 10.0.2.15 showed normal user behavior (svc_backup) and no suspicious network connections to critical subnets. Preventive actions included blocking the source IP at the firewall, resetting credentials for user CORP\helpdesk, and performing a full EPP scan with no threats found. Asset M2-5201 (decommissioned) was reconciled with external reference 203.0.113.41 in post-incident review.

Normal authentication event from 10.0.2.15 to internal gateway 10.0.1.1 by user CORP\helpdesk.
Incident response initiated. SIEM correlation confirms isolated scan event with no lateral movement to 10.0.12.0/24.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 45.33.32.156.
Credential reset for CORP\helpdesk initiated via IAM/PAM system.
Full EPP scan of WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15) completed with no threats detected.
Sandbox analysis of payload from initial scan confirms benign verdict (risk score 0.8).
Incident closed. Post-incident reconciliation includes decommissioned asset M2-5201 with external IP 203.0.113.41.

arguments.summary: A lateral movement attempt was detected originating from external IP 45.33.32.156, which previously conducted a port scan on internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). The attacker leveraged compromised credentials of the helpdesk account to move laterally into the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet. Immediate containment actions included blocking the malicious IP at the firewall, resetting credentials with MFA re-enrollment, and hardening the initially compromised endpoint. A cryptominer (Miner.CoinHive.A) was detected on WS-IT-101, indicating prior compromise. No data exfiltration or persistence mechanisms were identified during analysis. Asset M2-5201 (decommissioned) was reconciled with external reference 203.0.113.41 in post-incident review.

timeline.description: External IP 45.33.32.156 performed a port scan on WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15), detected and logged by IDS.
Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 to internal gateway (10.0.1.1) using CORP\helpdesk credentials.
Lateral movement detected into subnet 10.0.12.0/24; incident declared.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 45.33.32.156.
Helpdesk account password and MFA token reset; enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan initiated on WS-IT-101; cryptominer (Miner.CoinHive.A) detected in /tmp/.x11-lock.
Endpoint hardening playbook executed on WS-IT-101: SSH hardened, unnecessary services disabled, audit logging enabled.
Sandbox analysis confirmed file hash 92378156 as clean; no additional malware found.
Post-incident review completed. Asset M2-5201 reconciled with external reference 203.0.113.41.

arguments.summary: A credential theft incident was identified on host 10.0.5.20 (WS-FIN-042), where a user account (CORP\jsmith) was compromised via a phishing email containing a malicious attachment. This led to the execution of a PowerShell-based payload, resulting in a Cobalt Strike beacon connecting to external C2 infrastructure at 91.219.236.174. Attackers used stolen credentials for service accounts 'svc-backup' and 'svc-sql-prod' to perform lateral movement and maintain persistence. Immediate actions included resetting credentials, blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, and scanning the host. The decommissioned asset reference 203.0.113.42 has been included for reconciliation.

timeline.description: External IP 91.219.236.174 observed performing Nmap scan on internal host 10.0.2.15 (low-severity alert).
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.20).
Malicious PowerShell executed from Outlook process, launching encoded command.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing C2 beacon to 91.219.236.174.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
conditions:
  - CommandLine|contains: 'powershell'
  - ParentProcessName|endswith: 'outlook.exe'
  - CommandLine|contains: '-nop', '-w hidden', '-encodedcommand'
detection:
  selection:
    ParentProcessName|endswith: 'outlook.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-nop'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-encodedcommand'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
description: Detects obfuscated PowerShell launched directly from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

rule Suspicious_Outlook_Powershell_Delivery {
    meta:
        description = "Detects malicious Office documents delivering PowerShell payloads via DDE or macro"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1566.001"
        date = "2026-04-09"
    strings:
        $powershell_cmd = /powershell.*-nop.*-w hidden.*-enc/ nocase
        $outlook_parent = "outlook.exe" fullword ascii
        $rundll32_temp = "rundll32.exe" "\\Temp\\" fullword ascii
    condition:

arguments.summary: A network intrusion was detected originating from the external IP 198.51.100.23, identified as a Cobalt Strike C2 server. The initial compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) via a malicious rundll32 execution. The attacker attempted lateral movement via SMB and Kerberos TGT abuse. The source IP has been blocked at the firewall, the compromised user's credentials (CORP\jsmith) were reset, and the affected host was scanned and hardened. No data exfiltration was confirmed. Reconciliation includes decommissioned asset M2-5203 with external reference 203.0.113.43.

arguments.summary: A network intrusion was detected originating from external IP 198.51.100.23, identified as a Cobalt Strike beacon. The initial compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-042 via a malicious payload delivered through a suspicious rundll32 execution. The threat actor performed lateral movement attempts and established command-and-control (C2) communications. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the compromised user's credentials, and executing a remediation playbook across the affected host. The asset M2-5203 (decommissioned) was reconciled with external reference 203.0.113.43 as part of post-incident closure.

        all of them
}

arguments.summary: An investigation into a suspected APT-29 intrusion was initiated following detection of suspicious activity from external IP 203.0.113.88. Initial monitoring identified low-severity port scanning activity targeting a non-critical IT host (WS-IT-101). Analysis confirmed no malicious activity on the initially observed host. Subsequent administrative actions revealed malware on two engineering workstations (WS-ENG-022 and SRV-BUILD-01), including a high-severity keylogger. The external C2 IP was successfully blocked at the firewall. The incident is closed with no evidence of data exfiltration or lateral movement from the primary engineering assets.

Normal authentication event observed from WS-IT-101 to internal gateway.
Firewall rule deployed to block inbound traffic from 203.0.113.88.
Full EPP scans completed on affected engineering hosts. Keylogger detected on WS-ENG-022, adware on SRV-BUILD-01.

arguments.summary: An investigation into a suspected APT-29 campaign revealed a misidentified source IP. Initial telemetry pointed to external IP 203.0.113.88 as a C2 server, but subsequent analysis confirmed it was a benign IP associated with a decommissioned asset (M2-5204). The actual compromise originated internally from host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15), which had been used to conduct network reconnaissance and establish lateral movement. No malicious activity was found on the initially suspected hosts WS-ENG-015 and SRV-BUILD-01. A low-severity adware instance was identified and contained on SRV-BUILD-01 during remediation. The firewall rule blocking 203.0.113.88 has been revoked to prevent collateral impact. The incident is closed with a finding of internal misattribution.

timeline.description: IDS alert (IDS-2026-03200) triggered by scan from 203.0.113.88 to 10.0.2.15. Initially assessed as external reconnaissance.
Successful authentication from WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15) to internal router. Correlated with scan activity.
SIEM analysis reveals command execution with Base64-encoded payloads on SRV-BUILD-01 originating from WS-IT-101, not 203.0.113.88.
EDR confirms no malicious processes on WS-ENG-015. Sandbox analysis of retrieved artifacts returns clean verdict.
Firewall blocks 203.0.113.88 (later revoked). Full EPP scan of SRV-BUILD-01 detects and quarantines Adware.Agent.Y.
Incident re-scoped. True source identified as compromised WS-IT-101. Investigation transferred to internal threat team.

  service: netflow

level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/

deos:
  - name: Tenable Scanner
    condition:
      src_ip: '10.0.12.15'

arguments.summary: A credential compromise was detected on host WS-FIN-AP01, where user CORP\jsmith's Outlook process spawned a hidden PowerShell session executing a malicious encoded command. This led to the loading of an unsigned DLL via rundll32 from the Temp directory, establishing a C2 beacon to a known-bad external IP (185.220.101.42). The IP was previously observed conducting an Nmap scan against an internal IT host (WS-IT-101). Immediate actions included blocking the external IP at the firewall, resetting the user's password and MFA token, and conducting a full endpoint scan which detected a low-severity PUP. No evidence of data exfiltration was found, but persistence mechanisms may remain.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Spawned from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
conditions:
  - NewProcessName: '*\\outlook.exe'
  - CreatorProcessName: '*\\powershell.exe'
  - CommandLine: '*-enc*'
detection:
  selection:
    NewProcessName|endswith: '\\outlook.exe'
    CreatorProcessName|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
description: Detects PowerShell launched from Outlook with encoded command, a common phishing payload execution technique.

rule Suspicious_Rundll32_From_Temp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32 loading DLLs from user Temp directories"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $s1 = "rundll32.exe" fullword ascii
        $s2 = "\\Temp\\" fullword ascii
        $s3 = ".dll" fullword ascii
    condition:
        $s1 at 0 and $s2 and $s3
}

arguments.summary: A credential compromise was detected on host WS-FIN-AP01, originating from a phishing campaign. The attacker used a malicious email to deliver a PowerShell-based payload that launched a C2 beacon via rundll32.exe. The external C2 server (185.220.101.42) was blocked at the firewall, and the affected user's credentials were reset. No data exfiltration was confirmed, but lateral movement attempts were observed.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 performed an Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15).
Legitimate login from WS-IT-101 to domain controller (CORP\helpdesk).
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
Outlook spawned encoded PowerShell command (T1566.001).
PowerShell executed rundll32.exe to load unsigned DLL from Temp directory (T1218.011).
rundll32.exe established C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001).
Incident response initiated; firewall rule deployed to block 185.220.101.42.
User CORP\jsmith credentials and MFA reset.
Full EPP scan completed; one low-severity PUP detected and quarantined.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise was detected on host WS-FIN-AP01, originating from user CORP\jsmith's account. The compromise began with a phishing email triggering an encoded PowerShell script from Outlook, leading to the execution of a malicious DLL via rundll32.exe. The payload established C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad external IP (185.220.101.42). The attacker performed reconnaissance and attempted data exfiltration. Containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and scanning the host for malware. No data exfiltration was confirmed, but the account had access to sensitive financial data.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted an Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Alert logged as low severity.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
Encoded PowerShell command executed as child of Outlook, indicative of phishing payload (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned DLL from user's Temp directory, establishing C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1218.011, T1071.001).
Host file modification detected (T1565.001), likely to block security updates or redirect traffic.
Incident formally detected and investigated after alert correlation.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 185.220.101.42.
User CORP\jsmith's password and MFA token reset. Secure enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-AP01 completed, detecting a low-severity PUP in browser extensions.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 after a phishing email triggered malicious PowerShell execution from Outlook. The script deployed a reflective DLL via rundll32.exe, establishing C2 communication to 198.51.100.23:443. The attacker leveraged initial reconnaissance from IP 185.220.101.42, which previously conducted an Nmap scan against an internal IT host. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall and resetting the compromised user's credentials and MFA token. A full endpoint scan detected a low-severity PUP but no active malware persistence.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 performed Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged by IDS.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
Malicious encoded PowerShell executed as child of Outlook process.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, initiating C2 beaconing to 198.51.100.23:443.
Incident response initiated; EDR alerts confirmed suspicious process chain and network connections.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 185.220.101.42 and associated C2 infrastructure.
User CORP\jsmith password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-AP01 completed; detected PUP.Optional.BrowserHelper in browser extension.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise was detected on host WS-FIN-AP01, originating from a phishing campaign where a malicious PowerShell payload was executed from Outlook. The payload deployed a C2 beacon via rundll32.exe to external IP 185.220.101.42. The attacker conducted internal reconnaissance from a previously compromised IT workstation (WS-IT-101) that had been scanned from the same external IP. Immediate actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and executing a remediation playbook to isolate and scan the host.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted a port scan against WS-IT-101 (Ubuntu host in IT).
Successful internal authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller, suggesting lateral movement or credential misuse.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
Malicious encoded PowerShell command executed under user context, spawned by Outlook.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, establishing C2 beacon to 198.51.100.23:443.
Incident response initiated; C2 IP 185.220.101.42 blocked at firewall.
User CORP\jsmith's password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Full endpoint scan completed on WS-FIN-AP01; one low-severity PUP detected but unrelated.
Remediation playbook executed successfully on WS-FIN-AP01, including isolation, scan, and configuration hardening.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Spawned from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
conditions:
  - Image: '*\\outlook.exe'
  - Creator_Process_Name: '*\\powershell.exe'
  - Command_Line|contains: '-nop', '-w hidden', '-encodedcommand'
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\\outlook.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-nop'
      - '-w hidden'
      - '-encodedcommand'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566.001/
description: Detects obfuscated PowerShell execution from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 after a phishing email triggered malicious PowerShell execution from Outlook. The attacker used encoded commands to load an unsigned DLL via rundll32, establishing C2 communication with 198.51.100.23:443. The source IP 185.220.101.42 was previously observed conducting an Nmap scan against an internal IT host. Immediate containment actions included blocking the C2 IP at the firewall, resetting the user's credentials and MFA, and remediating the host via automated playbook. No evidence of data exfiltration was found.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 performed Nmap SYN scan against WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Logged by IDS.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook.exe on WS-FIN-AP01.
Malicious PowerShell spawned from Outlook with encoded command.
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned beacon.dll from Temp directory, initiating C2 beaconing to 198.51.100.23:443.
Incident response initiated based on detection of suspicious process chain.
Firewall rule deployed to block outbound traffic to 185.220.101.42 and 198.51.100.23.
User CORP\jsmith password and MFA token reset; secure enrollment link sent.
Automated remediation playbook executed on WS-FIN-AP01, isolating and cleaning host.
Full EPP scan completed; one low-severity PUP detected and quarantined.

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\\outlook.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566.001/
description: Detects encoded PowerShell execution from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.
